rationale: Amisulpride (D2/D3 antagonist, QTc risk, renal excretion) to lurasidone (D2, 5-HT2A, 5-HT7 antagonist, partial 5-HT1A agonist, low QTc risk). Common reason: QTc concerns with amisulpride — lurasidone is one of the antipsychotics with the least QTc effect. Also: desire for antidepressant augmentation profile (5-HT7 and 5-HT1A activity), or metabolic improvement (lurasidone weight-neutral). Critical prescribing note: lurasidone must be taken with food (≥350 kcal) for adequate bioavailability — patient education at initiation is essential. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start lurasidone 40 mg with the main meal. Continue amisulpride 400 mg. Counsel explicitly: lurasidone must be taken with at least 350 kcal of food — subtherapeutic levels result from fasted dosing.
Increase lurasidone to 80 mg with main meal. Plateau amisulpride. QTc: the total QTc burden is reducing as lurasidone does not prolong QTc; amisulpride risk remains until it is stopped.
Reduce amisulpride to 200 mg. Lurasidone at standard therapeutic dose. Monitor renal function (amisulpride is renally excreted — dose-reduce amisulpride taper further if eGFR <30).
Reduce amisulpride to 100 mg. EPS: lurasidone carries moderate EPS risk — monitor for stiffness, akathisia.
Stop amisulpride. Continue lurasidone 80 mg with main meal. Repeat ECG at 4 weeks to confirm QTc normalisation after amisulpride cessation.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Amisulpride 400 mg ≈ lurasidone 80 mg (inferred from DDD-method equivalences: both ≈ olanzapine 10 mg by proxy; limited direct data for lurasidone). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
